question: In October and November 2026, coordinated cyber-attacks targeted the connected refrigeration systems of hundreds of supermarkets and food logistics operators in Italy and at least nine other Member States, spoiling perishable foodstuffs, causing economic losses and threatening food security. Many of the compromised devices were obsolete, had not been updated and were vulnerable to hackers.
The Commission described these attacks as a deliberate attempt to target Europe’s food supply. In the light of the above, I ask the Commission: 1.

Will it urgently convene the European Food Security Crisis Preparedness and Response Mechanism (EFSCM) expert group and present an agri-food chain resilience action plan that coordinates the implementation of the NIS2 Directive and the Critical Entities Resilience Directive?

Will it provide financial support for SMEs in the agricultural, agri-food and logistics sectors or undertake any other initiatives to manage unsupported operational devices, none of which are covered by the Cyber Resilience Act?
Will it publish European guidelines on managing foodstuffs that have been exposed to cold chain disruptions and on using the Cyber Solidarity Act’s dedicated support toolkit for affected operators?
